assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly influential body of evidence and framework for understanding how technology, trade exposure, and task change reshape labour demand and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson are central, identifiable contributors to the task, polarization, and trade-shock evidence; the broader listed contribution has several related strands.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been tested across settings and have strongly shaped labour economics and policy debate over many years.
uncertainties: Separating the relative credit for technological change, trade shocks, and the broader inequality literature is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility and connected place, education, and policy to opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are especially central to the mobility atlas research program, with Katz an important contributor to foundational work.
assessment.maturity: The empirical approach is mature, widely adopted, and consequential for research and public policy.
uncertainties: The candidate label spans a large collaborative program, complicating a sharply bounded laureate set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of employer market power has substantially changed the interpretation of wages, employment, and labour-market institutions.
assessment.attribution: Manning is the clearest intellectual anchor for the monopsony framework, while Naidu is a major contributor to its modern empirical and policy development.
assessment.maturity: The literature has generated extensive empirical evidence and now informs central labour-policy questions.
uncertainties: Attribution between early theory, subsequent empirical measurement, and adjacent labour-market research remains contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work made asymmetric information in insurance empirically tractable and materially improved understanding of insurance-market design.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav, and Salanie represent complementary theoretical and empirical contributions to the stated discovery.
assessment.maturity: It is a well-established research agenda with durable influence in health, public, and insurance economics.
uncertainties: The theoretical and empirical contributions may be sufficiently distinct to make a single citation unusually broad.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life conditions and skill formation established that childhood environments have lasting economic consequences.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Almond are central to credible empirical evidence on early-life shocks, while Cunha is central to dynamic skill-formation theory.
assessment.maturity: The core conclusions are longstanding, influential, and supported by a broad subsequent literature.
uncertainties: The empirical early-life and structural skill-formation components have different intellectual lineages.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence methods supplied vivid, credible evidence of discrimination in labour markets and influenced empirical practice broadly.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are particularly closely associated with landmark experimental evidence; Charles is also an important contributor to discrimination research.
assessment.maturity: The methodology and its findings have been extensively replicated, extended, and integrated into labour economics.
uncertainties: The central contribution builds on earlier audit-study traditions, requiring careful historical attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural analysis of labour supply, taxes, and household decisions has delivered a major bridge between microeconomic theory, econometrics, and policy evaluation.
assessment.attribution: Blundell and Meghir are leading contributors to this sustained research program; MaCurdy has important foundational contributions.
assessment.maturity: The models and associated empirical methods have had long-running influence on public-finance and labour-policy analysis.
uncertainties: The contribution is diffuse across a broad structural-labour literature and may be hard to delimit as one discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Empirical work on taxable-income responses and optimal taxation has deeply influenced modern public economics and tax-policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Saez and Slemrod are especially central to the elasticity-of-taxable-income and optimal-taxation connection; Chetty made major related contributions.
assessment.maturity: The research has accumulated over decades and remains a core framework for interpreting tax responses.
uncertainties: Elasticities are sensitive to institutional context and interpretation, and the work overlaps with several adjacent tax-literature contributions.
